## (i) List the red cubes and find their total
Red cubes per trial (A to G): $0, 3, 2, 2, 4, 5, 1$.
\sum x &= 0 + 3 + 2 + 2 + 4 + 5 + 1
&= 17
## (i) Find the mean
\bar{x} &= \frac{\sum x}{n} = \frac{17}{7}
&= 2.42\ldots
&= 2.4
## (i) Find the sum of the squares of the red values
\sum x^2 &= 0^2 + 3^2 + 2^2 + 2^2 + 4^2 + 5^2 + 1^2
&= 0 + 9 + 4 + 4 + 16 + 25 + 1
&= 59
## (i) Find the variance
Use $\sigma^2 = \dfrac{\sum x^2}{n} - \bar{x}^2$.
\sigma^2 &= \frac{59}{7} - \left(\frac{17}{7}\right)^2
&= \frac{413}{49} - \frac{289}{49}
&= \frac{124}{49}
## (i) Find the standard deviation
\sigma &= \sqrt{\frac{124}{49}}
&= 1.59\ldots
&= 1.6
## (ii) Set up the correlation calculation
Let $x$ be the red cubes and $y$ the green cubes, with $n = 7$. Green cubes per trial: $4, 2, 0, 3, 0, 0, 2$.
\sum y &= 4 + 2 + 0 + 3 + 0 + 0 + 2
&= 11
\sum y^2 &= 16 + 4 + 0 + 9 + 0 + 0 + 4
&= 33
\sum xy &= 0(4) + 3(2) + 2(0) + 2(3) + 4(0) + 5(0) + 1(2)
&= 0 + 6 + 0 + 6 + 0 + 0 + 2
&= 14
## (ii) Substitute into the correlation formula
Use $\sum x = 17$, $\sum x^2 = 59$, $\sum y = 11$, $\sum y^2 = 33$, $\sum xy = 14$.
r &= \frac{n\sum xy - \sum x \sum y}{\sqrt{\left(n\sum x^2 - (\sum x)^2\right)\left(n\sum y^2 - (\sum y)^2\right)}}
&= \frac{7(14) - (17)(11)}{\sqrt{\left(7(59) - 17^2\right)\left(7(33) - 11^2\right)}}
&= \frac{98 - 187}{\sqrt{(413 - 289)(231 - 121)}}
&= \frac{-89}{\sqrt{124 \times 110}}
&= \frac{-89}{\sqrt{13640}}
&= -0.76204\ldots
&= -0.762
## (iii) Explain why the correlation is negative
Each trial picks exactly $5$ cubes, so the red, green and blue counts always add to $5$.
If a trial has more red cubes, there is less room for green cubes, so fewer green cubes are likely.
As the number of red cubes increases, the number of green cubes tends to decrease, so the correlation coefficient is negative.
ANSWER: \text{mean} = 2.4, \quad \sigma = 1.6, \quad r = -0.762

## 3 faces: the corners
A cube with $3$ faces outside sits at a corner of the cuboid. A cuboid has $8$ corners.
\text{3 faces} &= 8
## 2 faces: along the edges, not counting corners
There are $4$ edges of length $5$, $4$ of length $3$ and $4$ of length $4$. On each edge, remove the $2$ corner cubes.
\text{2 faces} &= 4(5 - 2) + 4(3 - 2) + 4(4 - 2)
&= 4(3) + 4(1) + 4(2)
&= 12 + 4 + 8
&= 24
## 1 face: the middle of each face
On each face, remove the border cubes, leaving a rectangle that is $2$ shorter in each direction. There are $2$ faces of each size.
\text{1 face} &= 2(5 - 2)(3 - 2) + 2(5 - 2)(4 - 2) + 2(3 - 2)(4 - 2)
&= 2(3)(1) + 2(3)(2) + 2(1)(2)
&= 6 + 12 + 4
&= 22
This matches the value given in the table.
## No faces: the hidden inside block
Remove the outer layer from every direction. The inside block is $2$ shorter in each dimension.
\text{no faces} &= (5 - 2)(3 - 2)(4 - 2)
&= 3 \times 1 \times 2
&= 6
## Check the total
8 + 24 + 22 + 6 &= 60
5 \times 3 \times 4 &= 60
ANSWER: \text{3 faces: } 8, \quad \text{2 faces: } 24, \quad \text{1 face: } 22, \quad \text{no faces: } 6

## Decide whether the statement is true or false
"If and only if" means the statement must work in both directions.
Vertically opposite angles are always equal, but equal angles need not be vertically opposite.
So the statement is false.
## Justify with a counter-example
In an equilateral triangle all three angles are $60^\circ$, so they are equal in size.
These angles are next to each other, not vertically opposite.
So equal angles are not always vertically opposite.
ANSWER: \text{False}

## Show two angles of the triangles are equal
$[GH]$ is parallel to $[AC]$, and $[BH]$ cuts across them.
|\angle EHD| &= |\angle DBC| = \theta
Reason: alternate angles.
|\angle EFD| &= \theta
Reason: given.
|\angle EFD| &= |\angle EHD|
## Show the angles at E are equal
|\angle FED| &= 90^\circ
Reason: angle of the rectangle.
|\angle HED| &= 90^\circ
Reason: $F$, $E$, $H$ lie on a straight line, so $\angle HED$ and $\angle FED$ add to $180^\circ$.
|\angle FED| &= |\angle HED|
## Show the angles at D are equal
The angles in each triangle add to $180^\circ$, and two angles in $FED$ equal two angles in $HED$.
|\angle FDE| &= |\angle HDE|
Reason: angles in a triangle sum to $180^\circ$.
## Show the triangles share a side
|ED| &= |ED|
Reason: common side.
## State the conclusion
Triangles $FED$ and $HED$ are congruent by ASA (angle, side, angle: the angles at $E$ and $D$ with the common side $[ED]$).
|FE| &= |EH|
Reason: corresponding sides of congruent triangles.
ANSWER: |FE| = |EH|

## Find |FE| using a parallelogram
$[AF]$ is parallel to $[BH]$ (equal angles $\theta$) and $[AB]$ is parallel to $[FH]$, so $ABHF$ is a parallelogram.
|FH| &= |AB| = 20
From part (i), $|FE| = |EH|$, so $|FE|$ is half of $|FH|$.
|FE| &= \frac{1}{2} \times 20
&= 10
## Find |FG|
$|GE| = |AC| = 20 + 30 = 50$.
|FG| &= |GE| - |FE|
&= 50 - 10
&= 40
## Set up a trigonometric equation in triangle AGF
$|\angle GFA| = \theta$, $|AG|$ is opposite $\theta$ and $|FG|$ is adjacent to $\theta$.
\tan\theta &= \frac{|AG|}{|FG|}
&= \frac{90}{40}
&= 2.25
## Solve for the angle
\theta &= \tan^{-1}(2.25)
&= 66.04\ldots^\circ
&\approx 66^\circ
ANSWER: \theta = 66^\circ

## Set up Pythagoras in the right-angled triangle
$[AB]$ is the hypotenuse.
|AC|^2 + 9^2 &= 70^2
## Find |AC|
|AC|^2 &= 70^2 - 9^2
&= 4900 - 81
&= 4819
|AC| &= \sqrt{4819}
## Find the gradient as a percentage
\text{gradient} &= \frac{|BC|}{|AC|} \times 100
&= \frac{9}{\sqrt{4819}} \times 100
&= 12.96\ldots
&\approx 13
ANSWER: 13\%

## Part (c): find a, the minimum of V
$\cos$ is largest ($1$) when $V$ is smallest.
a &= 2 - 0.4(1)
&= 1.6
## Part (c): find b, the maximum of V
$\cos$ is smallest ($-1$) when $V$ is largest.
b &= 2 - 0.4(-1)
&= 2.4
## Part (d): link V'(t) to breathing
$V'(t)$ is the rate of change of the volume of air in the lungs.
If $V'(t) > 0$, the volume is increasing, so Olga is breathing in.
If $V'(t) < 0$, the volume is decreasing, so Olga is breathing out.
ANSWER: a = 1.6,\ b = 2.4;\ V'(t) > 0 \text{ means breathing in},\ V'(t) < 0 \text{ means breathing out}

## Substitute t = 0.5 into V(t)
Set the calculator to radian mode.
V(0.5) &= 2 - 0.4\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} \times 0.5\right)
&= 2 - 0.4\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)
&= 1.7172\ldots
&\approx 1.717\ \text{litres}
ANSWER: 1.717\ \text{litres}

## Differentiate V(t)
The derivative of $\cos(kt)$ is $-k\sin(kt)$, and the constant $2$ differentiates to $0$.
V(t) &= 2 - 0.4\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}t\right)
V'(t) &= -0.4\left(-\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}t\right)\right)\frac{\pi}{2}
&= 0.2\pi\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}t\right)
## Substitute t = 0.5
V'(0.5) &= 0.2\pi\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} \times 0.5\right)
&= 0.2\pi\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)
&= 0.4442\ldots
&\approx 0.444\ \text{litres/second}
ANSWER: 0.444\ \text{litres/second}

## Find the maximum and minimum values
Breathes in fully: maximum $3.6$. Breathes out fully: minimum $1.3$.
## Find a, the midline
a &= \frac{3.6 + 1.3}{2}
&= 2.45
## Find b, the amplitude
Time $t$ starts when she has just breathed out fully, so $E$ starts at its minimum. A minimum at $t = 0$ means $b$ is negative.
|b| &= \frac{3.6 - 1.3}{2}
&= 1.15
b &= -1.15
## Find c from the period
At rest, the period is $\frac{2\pi}{\pi/2} = 4$ seconds. She breathes twice as often, so the period is $2$ seconds.
\frac{2\pi}{c} &= 2
c &= \pi
## Write the formula
E(t) &= 2.45 - 1.15\cos(\pi t)
ANSWER: E(t) = 2.45 - 1.15\cos(\pi t)

## Find the z-score
z &= \frac{x - \mu}{\sigma}
&= \frac{3.5 - 3.87}{0.36}
&= -1.03
## Use the normal tables with a positive z-score
The tables give $P(z < 1.03) = 0.8485$. By symmetry, $P(z < -1.03) = 1 - P(z < 1.03)$.
P(x < 3.5) &= P(z < -1.03)
&= 1 - P(z < 1.03)
&= 1 - 0.8485
&= 0.1515
ANSWER: 0.1515

## Write the confidence interval formula
A $95\%$ confidence interval uses $1.96$ standard errors.
\bar{x} &\pm 1.96\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}
## Find the margin of error
$\bar{x} = 3.74$, $\sigma = 0.36$, $n = 64$.
1.96 \times \frac{0.36}{\sqrt{64}} &= 1.96 \times \frac{0.36}{8}
&= 1.96 \times 0.045
&= 0.0882
## Find the lower limit
3.74 - 0.0882 &= 3.6518
## Find the upper limit
3.74 + 0.0882 &= 3.8282
ANSWER: 3.6518 \le \mu \le 3.8282

## State the hypotheses
H_0 &: \mu = 3.87
The null hypothesis says Galway players have the same mean score as players in Ireland.
H_1 &: \mu \neq 3.87
The alternative says the mean score is different.
## Compare the Irish mean with the confidence interval
From part (i), the $95\%$ confidence interval for the Galway mean is $3.6518 \le \mu \le 3.8282$.
The value $3.87$ is not inside this interval.
## State the conclusion and reason
Reject $H_0$ at the $5\%$ level.
Reason: $3.87$ is outside the $95\%$ confidence interval, so Galway players have a different mean score.
ANSWER: \text{Reject } H_0\text{: Galway players have a different mean score}

## Find the sample proportion and margin of error
The interval is centred on $\hat{p} = 0.35$ and its upper limit is $0.435$.
\text{margin} &= 0.435 - 0.35
&= 0.085
## Find p-hat times (1 - p-hat)
\hat{p}(1 - \hat{p}) &= 0.35 \times 0.65
&= 0.2275
## Set up the margin of error equation
1.96\sqrt{\frac{0.2275}{n}} &= 0.085
## Solve for n
\sqrt{\frac{0.2275}{n}} &= \frac{0.085}{1.96}
\frac{0.2275}{n} &= \left(\frac{0.085}{1.96}\right)^2
n &= \frac{0.2275}{\left(\frac{0.085}{1.96}\right)^2}
&= 120.96\ldots
&\approx 121
ANSWER: n = 121

## Fill in the 1st June branches
$80\%$ win, so the lose proportion is $1 - 0.8 = 0.2$.
360000 \times 0.8 &= 288000
360000 \times 0.2 &= 72000
## Find who plays on 2nd June
$90\%$ of winners play again and $25\%$ of losers play again.
288000 \times 0.9 &= 259200
72000 \times 0.25 &= 18000
## Split the 2nd June players into win and lose
Winning is independent of the previous day, so each group wins with proportion $0.8$ and loses with $0.2$.
259200 \times 0.8 &= 207360
259200 \times 0.2 &= 51840
18000 \times 0.8 &= 14400
18000 \times 0.2 &= 3600
## Find who plays on 3rd June
Use $0.9$ after a win and $0.25$ after a loss.
207360 \times 0.9 &= 186624
51840 \times 0.25 &= 12960
14400 \times 0.9 &= 12960
3600 \times 0.25 &= 900
ANSWER: \text{Tree completed as shown}

## Write the area of the square in terms of its side l
Area of a square is side times side.
l^2 &= 140
## Take the square root
l &= \sqrt{140}
&\approx 11.83
&\approx 11.8
ANSWER: l = 11.8\text{ cm}

## Write the cosine rule in triangle ADE
$\alpha$ is the angle at $A$, opposite the side $|ED| = 4$.
4^2 &= 6^2 + 8^2 - 2(6)(8)\cos\alpha
16 &= 36 + 64 - 96\cos\alpha
16 &= 100 - 96\cos\alpha
## Solve for cos alpha
96\cos\alpha &= 100 - 16
96\cos\alpha &= 84
\cos\alpha &= \frac{84}{96}
\cos\alpha &= \frac{7}{8}
## Take the inverse cosine
\alpha &= \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{7}{8}\right)
ANSWER: \alpha = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{7}{8}\right)

## Place Q on the unit circle using the angle
$|\angle QOP| = 45^\circ$ and $P = (-1, 0)$, so $OQ$ makes $135^\circ$ with the positive $x$-axis.
On the unit circle, a point at angle $\theta$ is $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$.
Q &= (\cos 135^\circ, \sin 135^\circ)
## Find the x co-ordinate
\cos 135^\circ &= -\cos 45^\circ
&= -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}
## Find the y co-ordinate
\sin 135^\circ &= \sin 45^\circ
&= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}
ANSWER: Q = \left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)

## Use similar triangles to set up an equation
Triangles $BDE$ and $BAC$ are similar. Let $|BE| = x$, so $|BC| = x + 10$.
Corresponding sides are in the same ratio: $|DE| = 12$ matches $|AC| = 15$.
\frac{x}{12} &= \frac{x + 10}{15}
## Solve for x
15x &= 12(x + 10)
15x &= 12x + 120
15x - 12x &= 120
3x &= 120
x &= 40
ANSWER: |BE| = 40\text{ cm}

## Find the lengths for the large and small cones
Large cone: radius $R = 15$, slant height $L = |BC| = 40 + 10 = 50$.
Small cone: radius $r = 12$, slant height $l = |BE| = 40$.
## Curved area of the basin is large cone minus small cone
\text{Curved} &= \pi R L - \pi r l
&= \pi(15)(50) - \pi(12)(40)
&= 750\pi - 480\pi
&= 270\pi
## Add the circular base
The basin has a base, so it counts in the total internal surface.
\text{Base} &= \pi r^2
&= \pi(12)^2
&= 144\pi
## Add the curved area and the base
\text{Total} &= 270\pi + 144\pi
&= 414\pi
&\approx 1300.6
ANSWER: \text{Total internal surface area} = 1300.6\text{ cm}^2

## Identify the shape of the net
Unrolled, the curved surface is a large sector (radius 50) with a smaller sector (radius 40) removed, both centred at $B$.
Radii are $|BE| = 40$ and $|BC| = 50$.
## Find the angle of the sector
The arc of the small sector (radius 40) equals the base circumference ($r = 12$).
\frac{\theta}{360} \cdot 2\pi(40) &= 2\pi(12)
\frac{\theta}{360} &= \frac{2\pi(12)}{2\pi(40)}
&= \frac{12}{40}
\theta &= 360 \times \frac{12}{40}
&= 108
## Draw the net
From $B$, draw two radii $108^\circ$ apart. Mark 40 cm and 50 cm along them.
Draw an arc of radius 40 and an arc of radius 50 between the radii, then join the ends.
The dashed lines from $B$ are construction lines, not part of the net.
ANSWER: \theta = 108^\circ,\ \text{radii } 40\text{ cm and } 50\text{ cm}

## Count the choices digit by digit
No digit repeats, so each place has one fewer choice than the last.
First digit has 9 choices, second 8, third 7, fourth 6.
\text{Codes} &= 9 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6
&= 3024
ANSWER: 3024

## Count the codes that contain a 2
The 2 can go in any of 4 positions.
The other 3 places are filled from the remaining 8 digits, with no repeats.
8 \times 7 \times 6 &= 336
## Multiply by the number of positions for the 2
4 \times 336 &= 1344
ANSWER: 1344

## List the sets of three different digits that can add up to a digit
The first three digits are different and add to the fourth digit, which is at most 9.
The smallest sum is $1 + 2 + 3 = 6$, so the fourth digit is 6 to 9.
1 + 2 + 3 &= 6
1 + 2 + 4 &= 7
1 + 2 + 5 &= 8
1 + 3 + 4 &= 8
1 + 2 + 6 &= 9
1 + 3 + 5 &= 9
2 + 3 + 4 &= 9
There are 7 sets, and the fourth digit is always new because it is bigger than each of the three.
## Count the orders for each set
The three digits can be arranged in $3!$ ways, and the fourth digit is fixed.
3! &= 6
## Multiply
7 \times 6 &= 42
ANSWER: 42

## Increase by 8% for 2020
An increase of 8% means multiply by $1.08$.
\text{Price at start of 2020} &= 240\,000 \times 1.08
&= 259\,200
## Increase by a further 9% for 2021
The 9% is based on the 2020 price, so multiply $259\,200$ by $1.09$.
\text{Price at start of 2021} &= 259\,200 \times 1.09
&= 282\,528
ANSWER: \text{2020: } €259\,200 \qquad \text{2021: } €282\,528

## Find the increase in value
\text{Increase} &= 472\,000 - 460\,000
&= 12\,000
## Write the increase as a percentage of the original value
Percentage increase $= \frac{\text{increase}}{\text{original}} \times 100$.
\text{Percentage increase} &= \frac{12\,000}{460\,000} \times 100
&= 2.608\ldots
&\approx 2.6\%
ANSWER: 2.6\%

## Substitute into the formula
F &= P\left(1 + \frac{r}{100}\right)^t
370\,000 &= 265\,000\left(1 + \frac{r}{100}\right)^4
## Isolate the bracket
Divide both sides by $265\,000$.
\left(1 + \frac{r}{100}\right)^4 &= \frac{370\,000}{265\,000}
Take the fourth root of both sides (the positive root, as the price is growing).
1 + \frac{r}{100} &= \sqrt[4]{\frac{370\,000}{265\,000}}
1 + \frac{r}{100} &= 1.08702\ldots
## Solve for r
\frac{r}{100} &= 1.08702\ldots - 1
r &= 100 \times 0.08702\ldots
r &\approx 8.7
ANSWER: r = 8.7\%

## Find the conjugate of z₁
$z_1$ is at $(3, -3)$, so $z_1 = 3 - 3i$. The conjugate changes the sign of the imaginary part.
z_1 &= 3 - 3i
\overline{z_1} &= 3 + 3i
## Plot the conjugate
$\overline{z_1}$ is the reflection of $z_1$ in the real axis: plot it at $(3, 3)$ and label it $\overline{z_1}$.
## Plot z₂ and z₃
Real part is the horizontal coordinate, imaginary part is the vertical coordinate.
z_2 &= 5 + i \quad\rightarrow\quad (5, 1)
z_3 &= 6 - 2i \quad\rightarrow\quad (6, -2)
Plot both points and label them $z_2$ and $z_3$.
ANSWER: \overline{z_1} = 3 + 3i \text{ at } (3,3);\; z_2 \text{ at } (5,1);\; z_3 \text{ at } (6,-2)

## Substitute z₂ and z₃
4z_2 - 5z_3 &= 4(5 + i) - 5(6 - 2i)
## Expand the brackets
&= 20 + 4i - 30 + 10i
## Collect real and imaginary parts
&= (20 - 30) + (4i + 10i)
&= -10 + 14i
ANSWER: -10 + 14i

## Recall what the modulus means
The modulus $|z|$ is the distance from the point to the origin.
## Compare the distances
On the diagram, $z_5$ is the point furthest from the origin, so tick the $z_5$ box.
## Give the reason
Reason: $z_5$ is the furthest point from the origin, so it has the largest modulus.
ANSWER: z_5 \text{ (it is the furthest point from the origin)}

## Expand the bracket
3(2x + 4) - 5 &= 3
6x + 12 - 5 &= 3
## Collect the numbers on the left
6x + 7 &= 3
## Move the numbers to the right-hand side
Subtract $7$ from both sides.
6x &= 3 - 7
6x &= -4
## Divide both sides by 6
x &= \frac{-4}{6}
x &= -\frac{2}{3}
ANSWER: x = -\frac{2}{3}

## (i) Real numbers up to 2.8
$x \in \mathbb{R}$ includes every point on the line. Put a closed dot at $2.8$ (because of $\le$) and shade to the left with an arrow.
## (ii) Integers up to 2.8
$x \in \mathbb{Z}$ means whole numbers only. Put a dot on each of $-4, -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2$ and continue to the left with an arrow. Do not shade between the dots.
## (iii) Natural numbers up to 2.8
$x \in \mathbb{N}$ means $1, 2, 3, \ldots$ (the scheme also accepts $0$). Only $1$ and $2$ are at most $2.8$, so put a dot on each of them and nothing else.
ANSWER: \text{(i) shaded line to } 2.8;\ \text{(ii) dots } \ldots,-1,0,1,2;\ \text{(iii) dots } 1, 2

## Tidy the first equation
x - y + 1 &= 0
x - y &= -1
## Multiply it by 4 so the y-terms match
The second equation has $4y$, so multiply the first by $4$.
4x - 4y &= -4
## Add the equations to eliminate y
(4x - 4y) + (2x + 4y) &= -4 + 19
6x &= 15
## Solve for x
x &= \frac{15}{6}
x &= \frac{5}{2}
## Substitute x into x - y + 1 = 0
\frac{5}{2} - y + 1 &= 0
\frac{5}{2} + 1 &= y
y &= \frac{7}{2}
ANSWER: x = \frac{5}{2},\quad y = \frac{7}{2}

## (i) Read off g(1.5)
Find $x = 1.5$ on the horizontal axis, go straight up to the curve, then across to the $y$-axis.
g(1.5) &= 2
## (ii) Find x when g(x) = -6
Find $y = -6$ on the vertical axis, go across to the curve (the left-hand part), then straight down to the $x$-axis.
x &= -2.8
## (iii) Count the real roots
Real roots are where the curve crosses the $x$-axis. Tick the box for $1$ root.
Reason: the graph cuts the $x$-axis only once.
ANSWER: g(1.5) = 2;\quad x = -2.8;\quad \text{1 real root (graph cuts the } x\text{-axis only once)}

## Read the local maximum
The local maximum is the top of the hump on the left, at about $x = -1.6$ and $y = -1$.
\text{Local maximum} &\approx (-1.6, -1)
## Read the local minimum
The local minimum is the bottom of the dip near the $y$-axis, at about $x = 0.25$ and $y = -3.1$.
\text{Local minimum} &\approx (0.25, -3.1)
ANSWER: \text{Max } (-1.6, -1);\quad \text{Min } (0.25, -3.1)

## Differentiate each term
Use $\frac{d}{dx}(x^n) = nx^{n-1}$, and the derivative of a constant is $0$.
h(x) &= x^3 + 2x^2 - x - 8
h'(x) &= 3x^2 + 4x - 1 - 0
h'(x) &= 3x^2 + 4x - 1
ANSWER: h'(x) = 3x^2 + 4x - 1

## Find the slope at x = 2
The slope of the tangent is $h'(2)$.
h'(2) &= 3(2)^2 + 4(2) - 1
&= 12 + 8 - 1
&= 19
## Use the point-slope formula
With $m = 19$ and point $(2, 6)$: $y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)$.
y - 6 &= 19(x - 2)
## Rearrange (optional)
y - 6 &= 19x - 38
0 &= 19x - y - 32
ANSWER: 19x - y - 32 = 0
